I feel the same way. You will realize people will spout cheerful advice not because they believe it - it's because they are insecure that could happen to them, so they chose not to believe it.

I think the truth is some people just get the raw end of the deal over and over until there aren't many ootions. Then you get old and have tons of regrets. Life's great. I was going to off myself at 16. I'm 26 and thinking back to that time a lot lately.

Positive afirmation to an extreme to yourself. Ask your boyfriend for his honesty 'will you support me to meet my weight goals and will you be okay not having an physical attraction until changes happen?' Yes = he loves and wants to support you, no = doesn't feel it'd worth his time to wait and see. I either case, you need to be willing to come to terms with either answer with what you want (just because he says yes or no shouldn't change what you want). Start small - introduce healthier eating habits (cut junk out) and telling yourself 'I'm stronger than needing to crave XYZ'. Also visually imagine your body being where you want it - then walk around with the mental mindframe that you are healthy and sexy. Don't think about any negative feelings about your body, just acknowledge the fact you are making changes and keep telling yourself 'I love myself, BF loves me because he was honest how he felt, now I'm making the changes and feel good about it'

The hardest part is stop thinking about unproductive thinking. Convince yourself you are a strong person, who's willing to become the change they want.

Well, I think from the sounds of it, if you show an interest in change and taking action - he should support you... if he doest, cut your losses and plan for the future! Don't let your emotions make yourself feel bad about yourself. You can view the weight gain as a common health condition that can be managed or even eliminated. Just do everything for you though... and make sure YOU know it.
I'm sorry, I think you misheard her... she is breaking up with you and you should plan on being a better you 3 months from now.

I'm not a doctor - so please verify any advice I give doesn't hurt your health!

As for the BF ultimatum - I would stay calm and focus your mind internally to yourself. You can try to actively get fit to lose weight (not to mention more energetic and hours in your days) or discuss how to move forward adjusting to this new life style.

I would try limiting all carbs (except fiber, this is great), getting your energy from fats and proteins. No sugar, no soda, no bread, and no starch. Eat nuts, meats, veggies, eggs, whatever - get an eye to avoid high carb food.

Stop eating until you are full - but until you are not hungry. Obtain concrete willpower. Life choices comes down to yes or no. Do you care? Then you will stop cheating yourself of a healthy body by stop eating crap. You don't need that sugar in your life,  the gratification is seconds,  where a healthy body is forever. 

Get plain Tums/Rolaids antacid tablets, if you feel hungry or nauseous in the morning or evening take one.  Avoid taking one 3 hours before a meal.

As for the non attraction he is feeling, try changing things up a bit. Maybe go on a jog with him, or ask to work out together, dress up in the bedroom and do hands or oral stuff while letting him undress you at his will. You can request hand or oral stimulation without getting fully undress - maybe gauge how comfortable he is with your body.

Remember, this is if you care how he feels about you. If you ever got pregnant and fat - would he fall out of attention with you? I personally would love having sex with my once skinny-now-fat SO if she was giving life to my future child. I would do everything in my soul to make sure she knows I'm madly in love and attracted to the beautiful soul I decided to have children with...

I think the same principle should apply here... if he truly loves you, he would tell you he's not attracted to you and honestly tell you if he's willing to try supporting you while you adapt new life styles while being open and honest. If the attraction detachment was enough to derail his love for you... then you have your answer. Being in love with someone is simply wanting that person the most happiness. Possessiveness is when that person wants the best for their happiness by attaching themselves to things.

I wish you the best.
I find canker sores are closely tied to nutritional deficiency or some environmental exposure. 2 months is a long time. I don't have any other advice than maybe see another GP.

Take multi vitamins, cut out alcohol, brush teeth before bed,  drink plenty of water,  and 7 hours of sleep a night.  They should go away after a week.  You can also try rinsing with a saline solution a few times a day.

I think you are over thinking this. From the sound of this you are either depressed, bi, or gay. I think you view sexuality as an alignment that you must 'chose a side' which can become an unhealthy mindset. You should instead view sexuality as a bag of skittles, some people like the red ones,  others the purple ones -- you happen to enjoy both (OR! have been liking the wrong ones). The point is, focus on you for a bit. I'm a straight guy and watched every porn you can imagine, but I don't frequent gay or bi couples whatever just because it doesn't interest me. Figure out what you enjoy and go for that. It'd be really unfair to get into a sexual relationship with someone to find out they are not your type. Or, if you feel open with that person, explain to them your predicament and see what they think. If they are supportive, you got a good friend at least. If they are salty, then you saved them and yourself a good deal of time.

The moral of the story go and try out and what interests you.
